facts_found: FREEZE is a temporary lock for a misplaced card; CLOSE is permanent deactivation and is the recommended action when the card is confirmed lost or stolen. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]
Freezing requires verified customer who owns the card and a card in ACTIVE status; freeze is performed with freeze_debit_card_3892 using the card_id. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

While frozen, all new transactions and recurring payments/subscriptions are declined, but already-authorized pending transactions may still process; the customer can unfreeze at any time by phone or in the mobile app. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]
Freezing does not block ATM access if the customer has the PIN; ATM access requires separately enabling 'ATM Block' in the mobile app. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

A frozen card that is not unfrozen within 90 days triggers a reminder notification; unfreezing uses unfreeze_debit_card_3893 and requires FROZEN status plus an OPEN linked checking account. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

Closing a debit card uses close_debit_card_4721 with parameters card_id and reason (lost, stolen, fraud_suspected, damaged, no_longer_needed, account_closing). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

Cards reported lost or stolen are closed immediately with no cooling-off period, are permanently deactivated and cannot be reactivated, and lost/stolen/fraud_suspected reasons bypass the 14-day minimum card age requirement. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

Closure requires the card be in ACTIVE or PENDING status with no pending/processing transactions and no pending refunds; pending refunds typically take 3-5 business days or the customer may acknowledge in writing that refunds will be credited to the linked checking account. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

After closing a lost/stolen card, the agent asks whether the customer wants a replacement ordered immediately, warns that pending transactions still process, that recurring payments must be updated, and that refunds to a closed card credit the linked checking account. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

For fraud_suspected closures the customer is advised to review recent transactions, file disputes for unauthorized charges, and change their online banking password. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

Replacement debit card policies vary by checking account tier; all shipping, design and excess-replacement fees are automatically charged to the linked checking account at order time and exact delivery_fee/design_fee amounts must be supplied to order_debit_card_5739. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

ENTRY TIER: maximum 2 replacement cards per rolling 12-month period, 48-hour waiting period after card closure before ordering, standard shipping only at delivery_fee $0, $25 excess replacement fee if the limit is exceeded. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

MID TIER: maximum 3 replacements per rolling 12 months, no waiting period, STANDARD delivery_fee $0 or EXPEDITED delivery_fee $15, $15 excess replacement fee over the limit. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

PREMIUM TIER: maximum 5 replacements per rolling 12 months, no waiting period, free expedited shipping (delivery_fee $0 for STANDARD and EXPEDITED), RUSH delivery_fee $35, no fee option if over the limit (must wait). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

ELITE TIER: unlimited replacements, no waiting period, delivery_fee $0 for STANDARD, EXPEDITED and RUSH, priority processing with cards shipping the same business day if ordered before 2pm EST. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

Design fees by tier: CLASSIC $0 for all tiers; PREMIUM metallic silver $10 for Entry/Mid and $0 for Premium/Elite; CUSTOM $25 for Entry/Mid, $15 for Premium, $0 for Elite. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

Replacement history is counted from cards with issue_reason 'lost', 'stolen', 'fraud' or 'damaged' issued in the last 12 months; 'new_account', 'first_card', 'expired', 'upgrade' and 'bank_reissue' do not count toward the limit. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029]

General debit card delivery options and timelines: STANDARD free 7-10 business days, EXPEDITED $15 3-5 business days, RUSH $35 1-2 business days (fees may vary by account tier); design options CLASSIC $0, PREMIUM $10, CUSTOM $25. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_023]

Debit card ordering eligibility: verified customer, checking account only (savings ineligible), OPEN status, account open at least 3 business days, maximum 1 active debit card per checking account, minimum $25 balance, customer at least 18, no pending order for the same account, and a valid US domestic address (no international shipping). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_023]

Expedited/rush fees are deducted automatically from the linked checking account and the order fails on insufficient funds; shipment can be tracked in the Rho-Bank mobile app. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_023]

A replacement debit card issued for lost/stolen/fraud must be activated with activate_debit_card_8292; after activation the agent reminds the customer to review recent transactions for unauthorized charges and to change the online banking password if fraud was suspected. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_024]

Previous debit cards linked to the same account are automatically deactivated when the new card is activated (reissued cards have a 24-hour grace period). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_024]

Regulation E limits customer liability for unauthorized debit card use to a maximum of $50 if reported within 2 business days, $500 if reported within 60 days, and potentially the full amount after 60 days. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Rho-Bank must investigate reported errors promptly (typically within 10 business days), report results within 3 business days, correct confirmed errors within 1 business day, and provide provisional credit within 10 business days for qualifying disputes. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Unauthorized debit card transactions can be reported 24/7 at 1-800-RHO-BANK, via the mobile app 'Report Issue' feature, or at rhobank.com/disputes; a police report is recommended for fraud over $500. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_036]

Provisional credit is required for qualifying disputes (timely reporting within 60 days of the statement date, eligible fraud/unauthorized dispute categories, a written statement, and an OPEN account with no holds) and is for the full disputed amount less any late-reporting liability offset of $50 or $500. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_032]

With provisional credit issued, the investigation window is 45 business days, extended to 90 days for international transactions, non-US POS transactions, or new accounts; reversal requires at least 3 business days' written notice. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_032]

Disputes are filed with file_debit_card_transaction_dispute_6281; card_present_fraud and card_not_present_fraud map to card_action 'close_and_reissue', while unauthorized_transaction maps to 'freeze_pending_investigation', and with multiple disputes the most severe card action is executed once for the card. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_031]

Dispute pre-filing limits: transaction at least $1.00, within 60 days, card linked to an OPEN checking account, and max open disputes per checking account tier of Entry 2, Mid 3, Premium 4, Elite 5 (limits are per account, not per customer). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_031]

Rho-Bank fraud detection applies customer-initiated and bank-initiated fraud alerts plus automatic velocity blocks that expire after 30 minutes; bank-initiated alerts cannot be cleared by agents and require security team review, and customers reporting transactions they did not make must be escalated. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

A card reported lost cannot be reactivated once reported; if the customer finds it, the agent checks for a PENDING replacement and helps order one if none exists. Stolen-card cases require enhanced identity verification (full name, DOB, last 4 of SSN, plus 2-3 recent transactions) and stolen cards cannot be reactivated. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Wallet-theft cross-product protocol: after the debit card freeze/close procedure, the agent must check for Rho-Bank credit cards with get_credit_card_accounts_by_user and proactively offer a replacement credit card with a new number, noting the offer if declined. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030]

Debit cards are retrieved per checking account with get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823(account_id), returning card_id, account_id, user_id, status (ACTIVE, PENDING, FROZEN, CLOSED), issue_reason, date_issued, card_design and daily limits; all of a customer's checking/savings accounts come from get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847(user_id). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

If a customer insists they never reported a card stolen, that is a major security flag requiring transfer to the security team rather than self-resolution. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Emergency replacement of a lost/stolen card while abroad can typically arrive within 2 days subject to local courier availability; a cashier's check is available for an $8 fee for access to funds while waiting. [doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_007]

get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823 only returns debit cards for checking accounts (savings accounts do not have debit cards) and returns an empty list when no cards exist for the given account_id. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

All documented debit-card workflows (order, activate, freeze/unfreeze, close, PIN reset, limit increase, decline-code triage) obtain card_id by first looking up the checking account and then listing cards for that account_id — none key off user_id or last-4. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847(user_id) is the documented tool for retrieving a customer's bank accounts (checkings and savings) and is the only such 'Retrieving Customer Account Information' tool in the KB; it returns account_id, account_type, account_class, status, balance, date_opened. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

Debit-card procedures state that all of a customer's checking/savings accounts come from get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847(user_id), confirming there is no second account-ID discovery path. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]

Decline-code troubleshooting instructs agents to 'look up the debit cards for the account' and to 'look up the customer's accounts' — i.e., last-4 matching is done manually against the per-account card list, not via a card-number search tool. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

The only user_id-keyed card account lookup documented is get_credit_card_accounts_by_user, which returns credit card accounts (active and closed) only, not checking accounts or debit cards. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030]

The only 'last 4' tool in the KB is get_card_last_4_digits(credit_card_account_id), which is a credit-card tool that returns last-4 from a known credit card account ID — it does not work in reverse and does not apply to debit cards. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_013]

Downstream debit-card action tools all require card_id (e.g., close_debit_card_4721(card_id, reason), freeze_debit_card_3892(card_id), unfreeze_debit_card_3893(card_id), clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892(card_id, reason), request_temporary_debit_card_limit_increase_8374(card_id, limit_type, new_limit), reset_debit_card_pin_6284(card_id, last_4_digits, new_pin)), so card_id must come from the account-keyed lookup. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_040]

PIN reset takes card_id plus last_4_digits as a verification input, not as a lookup key — further evidence last-4 is used to confirm identity, not to find a card. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_027]

get_bank_account_transactions_9173 requires a known account_id and does not return account records by user_id, so it cannot substitute for the account lookup. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_018]

Customers can unfreeze a card at any time by calling customer service or through the mobile app; the app is documented for unfreezing, not for the initial freeze. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

A card freeze does not block ATM access if the customer has the PIN; for ATM blocking the customer must separately enable 'ATM Block' through the mobile app. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]
If the customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, the documented recommendation is to CLOSE the card rather than freeze it. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

Lost/stolen/fraud card closure is an agent-side procedure using close_debit_card_4721(card_id, reason); lost or stolen cards are closed immediately with no cooling-off period and cannot be reactivated. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_025]

Replacement debit cards are ordered by the agent via order_debit_card_5739 after eligibility checks; no customer self-service ordering flow is documented. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_023]

The lost/stolen cross-product protocol directs the AGENT to complete the debit card freeze/close procedure and then check credit cards with get_credit_card_accounts_by_user; it is not a customer self-service flow. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030]

The 'Report Issue' app feature is documented for reporting unauthorized transactions (disputes), not for locking/freezing or reporting a card lost/stolen. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_036]

facts_found: Fraud alerts are flags placed on debit cards; two types exist: customer-initiated (clearable by customer service after identity verification) and bank-initiated (placed by Rho-Bank's fraud detection systems, CANNOT be cleared by customer service agents and require review by the security team). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Velocity blocks are automatic temporary holds that expire after 30 minutes and can be cleared earlier by a customer service agent after identity verification. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Tool: clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892(card_id, reason) clears fraud alerts or velocity blocks on a customer's debit card; it CANNOT clear bank-initiated fraud alerts and will return an error if attempted, in which case the customer must be transferred to the security team. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

The debit card lookup response exposes a fraud_alert_active field and an alert_source field; if fraud_alert_active is TRUE and alert_source is 'bank_initiated' the agent must NOT clear it and must transfer to human agents (security team). If alert_source is 'customer_initiated', the agent asks the customer to verify recent transactions and then clears the alert. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]
The same debit card lookup response exposes a velocity_blocked field used to detect temporary velocity blocks. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823(account_id) is the debit card lookup that returns card_id and card attributes; it is keyed only by account_id (no user_id- or last-4-keyed debit card search), and returns an empty list if no cards exist for the account. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]
The customer's bank accounts (and therefore account_id values) are retrieved with get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847(user_id). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

Before using clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892 the agent must always verify the customer's identity and document why the alert/block was cleared in the interaction notes. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Escalate to the security team when the fraud alert is bank-initiated, the customer cannot verify identity, the customer reports transactions they did not make, the caller may not be the account holder, or the explanation for unusual activity is suspicious/inconsistent. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

For PIN locks, pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' means the card cannot be unlocked by chat agents and must be offered for transfer to the security team; another card having an active fraud alert adds +2 to the fraud risk score (i.e., fraud alert state is read from card data, not from a separate alert-query tool). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_041]

Codes 34 and 59 (suspected fraud) and codes 04/07 (capture/pick up card) are internal-only: the agent must NOT attempt to clear or explain them, must not tell the customer the card was flagged for fraud, and should use transfer_to_human_agents / branch referral. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

The KB documents fraud-alert flags and a fraud-alert clearing tool only for debit cards; credit-card documentation covers real-time monitoring alerts and customer in-app lock (Platinum Rewards) and replacement ordering, but no agent-side credit-card fraud-alert check or clear tool. get_credit_card_accounts_by_user is documented only to retrieve credit card accounts for the cross-product security check. The freeze tool freeze_debit_card_3892(card_id) requires the card to be in ACTIVE status and requires a card_id, which cannot be obtained when the account/card lookup returns no records — the practical reason the request cannot be completed in-chat. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026]

Regulation E limits debit-card liability to $50 if unauthorized use is reported within 2 business days, $500 within 60 days, and potentially unlimited after 60 days — supporting the time-sensitive framing of urgent lost-card protection. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Bank-initiated fraud alerts cannot be cleared by customer service agents and require transfer to the security team; escalation to the security team is also required when the customer cannot verify identity or reports transactions they did not make. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Escalation is warranted for security concerns such as suspected unauthorized access or account-access lockouts, per the checking-accounts troubleshooting FAQ. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_002]

Fraud alerts are flags placed on debit cards; two types exist: customer-initiated (clearable by customer service after identity verification) and bank-initiated (placed by Rho-Bank's fraud detection systems, CANNOT be cleared by customer service agents and require review by the security team). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Velocity blocks are automatic temporary holds that expire after 30 minutes and can be cleared earlier by a customer service agent after identity verification. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Tool: clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892(card_id, reason) clears fraud alerts or velocity blocks on a customer's debit card; it CANNOT clear bank-initiated fraud alerts and will return an error if attempted, in which case the customer must be transferred to the security team. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

The debit card lookup response exposes a fraud_alert_active field and an alert_source field; if fraud_alert_active is TRUE and alert_source is 'bank_initiated' the agent must NOT clear it and must transfer to human agents (security team). If alert_source is 'customer_initiated', the agent asks the customer to verify recent transactions and then clears the alert. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]
The same debit card lookup response exposes a velocity_blocked field used to detect temporary velocity blocks. [doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003]

get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823(account_id) is the debit card lookup that returns card_id and card attributes; it is keyed only by account_id (no user_id- or last-4-keyed debit card search), and returns an empty list if no cards exist for the account. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_028]
The customer's bank accounts (and therefore account_id values) are retrieved with get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847(user_id). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_009]

Before using clear_debit_card_fraud_alert_4892 the agent must always verify the customer's identity and document why the alert/block was cleared in the interaction notes. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

Escalate to the security team when the fraud alert is bank-initiated, the customer cannot verify identity, the customer reports transactions they did not make, the caller may not be the account holder, or the explanation for unusual activity is suspicious/inconsistent. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

For PIN locks, pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' means the card cannot be unlocked by chat agents and must be offered for transfer to the security team; another card having an active fraud alert adds +2 to the fraud risk score (i.e., fraud alert state is read from card data, not from a separate alert-query tool). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_041]

Codes 34 and 59 (suspected fraud) and codes 04/07 (capture/pick up card) are internal-only: the agent must NOT attempt to clear or explain them, must not tell the customer the card was flagged for fraud, and should use transfer_to_human_agents / branch referral. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

The KB documents fraud-alert flags and a fraud-alert clearing tool only for debit cards; credit-card documentation covers real-time monitoring alerts and customer in-app lock (Platinum Rewards) and replacement ordering, but no agent-side credit-card fraud-alert check or clear tool. get_credit_card_accounts_by_user is documented only to retrieve credit card accounts for the cross-product security check.
